dedupe_keys.name: risk data library standard rdls for hazard exposure vulnerability and loss metadata

description: The Risk Data Library Standard is an open metadata standard for describing disaster and climate risk datasets, covering the four components of risk analysis: hazard, exposure, vulnerability and loss. Version 1.0.0 is a data model of common core metadata for all risk datasets plus specific metadata for each component, so that risk datasets from different producers can be catalogued and compared consistently, with documentation hosted at docs.riskdatalibrary.org. It is curated by the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery at the World Bank. The schema and documentation are available free on GitHub under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence given in the repository. Caveats: it describes metadata, not the risk data themselves, and its value depends on data publishers adopting it. It helps infrastructure risk modellers find and match hazard, exposure and fragility inputs and document their own model inputs and outputs in a shared form; a related record is the ThinkHazard screening tool, also from GFDRR.
